text:
incident-bot: :rotating_light: [P0] Aurum Insurance (dedicated VPC) — eu-west-1 dedicated pool "aurum-eu-west1-pool" p99 latency spike observed. p99 = 3.1s (SLO 1.5s). Alert window started ~12:21 UTC. Error rate low, retries up slightly. Triggering war room.
ryan_sre: on it. paging leah_oncall for primary response.
leah_oncall: saw the page, joining. what's the traffic pattern? any deploys?
sam_prodeng: no deploys in last 6h. Customer routes mostly short-chat flows. We saw a big jump in seq length on a few tenants around 12:15.
maya_support: customer-reported timeouts to their app at ~12:25. They opened a ticket. Account team looped in.
ops_pager: current affected routes: /v1/chat/stream (aurum tenant id = ten-aur-001). Throughput same, latency up. KV cache hit % dropped 28% for this tenant.
ryan_sre: KV cache dropped — suspect cache eviction path or cold KV after model switch. Any recent model variant rollouts for aurum?
sam_prodeng: aurum pinned to rwd-3b-q4 (quantized). No recent rollouts. But we did enable global cache eviction policy change earlier today (12:00) — could be related.
leah_oncall: ok immediate mitigations: 1) move aurum traffic to warm pool in eu-west-2 (failover) 2) pin to older KV snapshot if available 3) temporarily reduce max_seq for aurum to 512 to avoid very long requests. Which is fastest?
ryan_sre: fastest is routing to eu-west-2 warm failover. Can we do a region failover for a dedicated pool without customer signoff? per contract we can failover for SLO/resilience.
jess_pm: confirm: account notified? we should mention impact and ask permission if we plan any heavier changes beyond routing.
maya_support: logged PSR and told customer we're investigating. they want ETA on mitigation.
leah_oncall: doing routing now. running plan: set route override -> eu-west-2 fallback, scale pool replicas up by +2 in eu-west-2, enable per-tenant throttling at 10rps for background jobs.
leah_oncall: /run-stage: route-override --tenant ten-aur-001 --from eu-west-1 --to eu-west-2 --ttl 30m
deploy-bot: command accepted. creating route override: override-id ov-1995-aurum-1.
ryan_sre: scaling eu-west-2 warm pool: kubectl -n dedicated scale deployment/aurum-eu-west2-pool --replicas=5
```
scaled deployment "aurum-eu-west2-pool" to 5
```
ops_pager: KV cache warmup starting. prefetching common prefixes for tenant.
sam_prodeng: also dropping model batch size for aurum to 1 and disable large-context attention optimizations for the pinned model — safer for latency.
leah_oncall: throttles in place. monitoring p95/p99 now.
incident-bot: update: route override created; eu-west-2 pool scaled; warming KV. Next check in 5m.
ryan_sre: quick health dump from eu-west-2 pool:
```
pool: aurum-eu-west2-pool
replicas: 5
avg_latency_p95: 420ms
avg_latency_p99: 1.1s
cpu: 72%
gpu_mem: 68%
kv_hit: 84%
```
ryan_sre: initial numbers look good, p99 down from 3.1s -> 1.1s on failover.
maya_support: passing to customer: mitigation in place, we expect normal traffic within 5-10m.
jess_pm: ok keep account updates every 15m. Sam, follow up on why KV eviction happened.
sam_prodeng: digging into eviction logs now. seeing a config roll earlier (12:00) that reduced global cache budget for quantized models. I think that cut caused tenant working set thrash.
leah_oncall: action items: 1) revert cache budget change for quantized models to previous value 2) run postmortem for config gating 3) validate failover runbook and per-tenant routing TTLs
ryan_sre: reverting config: /infra/ops config-set cache.global_quantized_budget=0.22 -> 0.30 (previous). deploy-bot: applying...
deploy-bot: config update applied, rolling restart not required.
ops_pager: KV hit recovered to 92% for aurum after config revert + warmup. p99 now ~480ms in eu-west-2, eu-west-1 still degraded but traffic is routed.
leah_oncall: marking incident as mitigated (customer routed successfully, p99 under SLO on failover). Keeping war room open for root cause and remediation.
incident-bot: incident timeline recorded. severity P0 -> mitigated state. incident start 1995012345, mitigated 1995013450.
jess_pm: customer update sent: "We've routed your traffic to a warm failover region and reverted a cache config change while we investigate root cause. We will follow up with a postmortem and timeline."
ryan_sre: next steps: postmortem owner = sam_prodeng, deep dive KV budgets & rollout gating, add canary checks for cache budget changes.
leah_oncall: handing off to morning on-call (ryan) at 07:00 UTC for monitoring and RCA progress. I'll update runbook with lessons.
ryan_sre: accepted handoff. I'll coordinate with Sam and Maya and schedule postmortem.
maya_support: will send customer timeline + internal bridge notes.
leah_oncall: closing warroom in 30m unless something regresses. great job everyone. :thumbsup:
